title: Real-Time Collaborative Document Canvas in TypeScript with Yjs CRDTs, WebSockets & IndexedDB Offline Sync
problem: Collaborative web applications (digital whiteboards, multi-cursor document editors, and design canvases) suffer from text jumping, cursor desynchronization, and silent data loss when multiple users edit concurrently over high-latency or intermittent networks. Centralized lock-based synchronization introduces unacceptable UI freezes, while naive operational transformation (OT) engines require complex central coordination servers that fail when network connections drop. This project builds a production-grade real-time collaborative document and canvas editor in TypeScript and React. The system resolves concurrent character and geometric mutations deterministically using Yjs Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs), streams binary update vectors over WebSockets with sub-25ms latency, stores local document snapshots and uncommitted deltas in IndexedDB, and renders multi-peer awareness presence cursors with zero layout stutter.

use_cases.title: Cross-Functional Digital Architecture Whiteboard
use_cases.first_sentence: Distributed engineering and design teams sketching system architecture diagrams need to co-edit geometric nodes and connectors simultaneously without locking.
use_cases.second_sentence: The canvas syncs Yjs shared map data structures over WebSockets, converging node positions deterministically even when two engineers move the same node concurrently.

use_cases.title: Multi-Author Collaborative Rich-Text Policy Drafting
use_cases.first_sentence: Legal counsel and compliance officers co-drafting regulatory compliance policies need seamless real-time typing with character-level attribution.
use_cases.second_sentence: The editor binds Yjs shared text types to rich-text views, rendering peer presence cursors and merging concurrent typing deltas without character transposition.

use_cases.title: Offline-to-Online Field Operations Report Collaboration
use_cases.first_sentence: Emergency response coordinators drafting incident mitigation plans frequently lose Wi-Fi connectivity while walking between disaster command centers.
use_cases.second_sentence: The web app persists document updates locally in IndexedDB, automatically synchronizing state vectors and converging with remote edits upon network reconnection.

hard_parts: Integrating Yjs binary CRDT state vector encoding with custom React state hooks without causing excessive DOM re-renders during high-frequency typing
Managing ephemeral user awareness states (cursor coordinates, active selection spans, user profile avatars) over WebSockets with automatic timeout cleanup
Designing an IndexedDB storage adapter that caches compact document snapshots and replays uncommitted CRDT delta buffers upon browser reload
Handling complex concurrent editing conflicts (simultaneous text insertions, deletions, and block repositioning) while maintaining mathematical convergence across 50 simulated clients
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating React canvas UI components, Yjs CRDT state bindings, WebSocket room synchronizers, and IndexedDB storage adapters
Multi-client concurrent chaos test report proving 100 of 100 simulated conflicting edits converge to mathematically identical document state across 5 concurrent peers

Anti-fake verification script simulating two partitioned clients concurrently inserting conflicting words at index 0, reconnecting, and asserting identical converged text across both browser instances

architecture.data_flow: A user types a character in the React editor; the local Yjs binding generates a compact binary update vector and writes it to IndexedDB in < 10ms; the WebSocket synchronizer streams the binary payload over WebSockets; the Node.js room coordinator verifies the frame, saves it to the document update log, and broadcasts the frame to all other peers in the room; remote peers apply the update to their local Y.Doc instances, which deterministically merges the change and updates the React DOM via Yjs event listeners; simultaneously, mouse movements stream awareness updates (x, y coordinates) to render animated peer cursor flags.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Mathematically proven commutative, associative, and idempotent CRDT merge operations eliminating conflict resolution ordering dependencies.

riskiest_component.name: Memory Leaks and Tombstone Bloat in CRDT History Logs
riskiest_component.mitigation: Execute periodic server-side Yjs document compaction and snapshotting to prune unreferenced deletion tombstones.
riskiest_component.fallback: Client-side state vector catch-up discarding delta history older than 7 days.
